revisions: Event-id self-consistency is insufficient for chain integrity: a tampered event can name a different otherwise-valid predecessor and still have a perfectly recomputable current hash.

Anchored chain verification must compare the envelope predecessor_event_id to the locally trusted predecessor event id after current-envelope validation/hash recomputation and fail closed on mismatch.
candidate_revision: Add an explicit trusted-predecessor anchor check to the restricted synthetic event verifier. A current event is accepted only when its own canonical hash recomputes and its predecessor_event_id equals the trusted predecessor id; recomputing a new current hash after substituting a different valid predecessor does not preserve chain validity.
